newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Former Prime Minister and opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia said on Sunday that people would not allow Bangladesh to be used to supress the struggle for independence in the seven north-eastern states of India.
Foreign Secretaries of the four countries of the planned sub-regional cooperation are expected to meet in Kathmandu in late March to draw the outlines for its founding.
An ammendment bill will be placed in the Parliament to toughen the existing environment protection laws spelling stringent punishment for the violators.
Bangladesh has so far treated some 849 patients affected by arsenic contamination of sub-soil water.
The U.S. State Department, in its 1996 country report on human rights practices, has highly commended Bangladesh's judiciary, saying the legal system in Dhaka enjoys "high degree of independence".
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, now visiting the United States, on Sunday urged the expatriate Bangladeshis to invest back home.
The government has decided to mobilise Taka 5 billion for setting up composite textile mills and other backward linakage industries for knitwear and readymade garments.
Bangladesh and Romania on Sunday signed an agreement for bolstering their bilateral trade relations.
